segments.text:
build12.sh writes this line before it compiles.
- `host=ubuntu`: the host name that the build machine (CRB) reports.
- `utc=`: the start time, 2026-11-15 at 17:12:11 UTC.
- `load_before=`: the load average of the last 1, 5 and 15 minutes: 1.18, 28.51 and 31.03 tasks.
- `logins=0`: the command `who` listed no logged-in user.
The 5-minute and 15-minute values are far above the 1-minute value. So other work had loaded the machine some minutes before the build.
segments.heading: Lines 1 to 5: machine, compiler, flags, compiler messages

segments.text: `cc=`: the first line that `gcc --version` printed. The compiler is gcc 14.2.0. The build of bw_old and bw_new on 2026-11-13 recorded the same version line [Ref2].

The flags of the compile command. The first seven are the flags of the bw_old and bw_new build [Ref2]. That build does not have the last three. The build scripts of the runner programs bwx, bwx8, bwx10, bwx11 and bwx12 hold the same ten flags [Ref1].
- `-O3`: optimisation level 3 of gcc.
- `-march=native`: gcc may use every instruction of the CPU that it runs on (here a CPU of CRB).
- `-fno-tree-loop-distribute-patterns`: gcc does not replace a loop by a call of a library function such as `memset`.
- `-pthread -Wall -Wextra -std=gnu11`: thread support, the usual and the extra warnings, the C language of 2011 with GNU extensions.
- `-fno-ipa-icf`: gcc does not merge two functions that have the same code. bwx12.c holds some kernels twice under two names [Ref4].
- `-fno-toplevel-reorder -falign-functions=4`: gcc keeps the functions in the order of the source file and aligns a function start to 4 bytes only. bwx12.c needs both to put each kernel at a chosen address modulo 64 [Ref4].
build12.sh appends every message of gcc (warnings and errors) between these two lines. Nothing stands between them: gcc printed no message.

build12.sh ran `bwx12 --selftest` and saved the output in selftest-bwx12.txt.
- `exit=0`: the exit status of that run. The self-test returns 0 when no check failed [Ref7].
- `# failures=0`: the last line of the saved output, copied here.
The saved output holds 457 check rows, and each one ends with `pass` [Ref6]. 422 of them check what a kernel reads, writes or returns. The other 35 check the trial mode and the table of kernels in bwx12.c. No check concerns a rate.
segments.heading: Line 6: self-test

segments.text:
build12.sh disassembles the function `timed_sequence`. It counts the branch and call instructions whose target lies outside the function, per target [Ref5].
- `(indirect)=4`: 4 calls through a register. They are the kernel calls: a kernel is called through a function pointer, and the code has one such call per kernel type (read, old read, write, copy) [Ref4].
- `clock_gettime=2`: 2 calls of the clock read.
- `tcount=2`: 2 instructions that go to `tcount`, the function that reads the hardware counters.
- `__stack_chk_fail=1`: 1 call of the function that the compiled code calls when its stack guard check fails.
Any other target stops the build with exit status 6. The build also stops with status 6 when `clock_gettime` or the indirect call is missing. `timed_sequence` belongs to the trial mode. The whole-chip test does not run it.
segments.heading: Lines 7 and 8: calls inside the timed functions (trial mode)

segments.text: The same count for `timed_sequence_hot`, the variant of `timed_sequence` for the option `--hot-copy` of the trial mode. The targets and the counts equal line 7. The whole-chip test does not run this function.

build12.sh reads the symbol table of the new binary with `nm`. For five functions it prints the start address modulo 64.
- `call=24`: the function through which a thread calls a kernel.
- `read_smaps=52`: the function that reads the page state of the buffers from /proc/self/smaps.
- `tcount=52`, `timed_sequence=28`, `timed_sequence_hot=32`: functions of the trial mode.
In the source of the interval mode, `worker` calls `call` inside a timed interval, and `main` calls `read_smaps` between two intervals [Ref4].
bwx12.c adds unused bytes after its kernels so that these functions start at the same address modulo 64 as in bwx8, bwx10 and bwx11 [Ref4].
segments.heading: Lines 9 to 15: placement of five functions, modulo 64

segments.text: Line 10: the same values for the accepted binary of bwx8. build12.sh reads that binary with `nm` and does not run it. bwx8 has no `timed_sequence_hot`. Line 11: `same` means that the four values of bwx8 equal the first four values of line 9. A difference would print `DIFFERS`. It would not stop the build.
The same for the accepted binary of bwx10. `same`: all five values equal line 9.
The same for the accepted binary of bwx11. `same`: all five values equal line 9.
The title of the next seven lines. They are the output of `sha256sum`: the sha256 digest (64 hexadecimal digits), two blanks, the file name.
segments.heading: Lines 16 to 23: sha256 digests

segments.text: The three inputs of the build: the C source of bwx12, the self-test source that bwx12.c includes, and the build script.

The digest of the binary `bwx12`. The whole-chip test of 2026-11-17 ran a binary with this digest. go.sh and go2.sh hold the digest and stop before the first run if the binary has another one. rx.sh checks it again when it starts and writes it to env.txt [Ref3].

Three outputs of the build: listing.txt (the machine code of every kernel as text), offsets.tsv (the loop start of every kernel) and seq-listing.txt (the machine code of `timed_sequence` and `timed_sequence_hot`).
`load_after=`: the load average at the end, in the form of line 1. `utc=`: the end time, 17:12:14 UTC. That is 3 seconds after the time of line 1.
